primary.title: The Four Voyages of Christopher Columbus
primary.author: Christopher Columbus
primary.rationale: This is a collection of letters and journal entries attributed to Columbus detailing his voyages. The first letter, describing his initial discoveries, is particularly famous.

primary.title: The Journal of Christopher Columbus
primary.author: Christopher Columbus
primary.rationale: The original journal is lost, but it was transcribed by Bartolomé de las Casas. This is a primary account of his first voyage.

primary.title: Letter from Christopher Columbus to Luis de Santángel
primary.author: Christopher Columbus
primary.rationale: A significant letter written shortly after his first voyage, informing the Spanish Crown's treasurer of his discoveries.

secondary.title: 1491: New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus
secondary.author: Charles C. Mann
secondary.rationale: While not solely about Columbus, this book provides essential context for the Americas prior to European contact, offering a critical perspective on the impact of Columbus's voyages.

secondary.title: Columbus: The Four Voyages
secondary.author: Laurence Bergreen
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography that draws on Columbus's own writings and other historical documents to provide a detailed account of his life and voyages.

secondary.title: The Lost History of the Americas
secondary.author: Felipe Fernández-Armesto
secondary.rationale: This work offers a broad historical sweep of the Americas, placing Columbus's arrival within a much larger narrative of human history and interaction.

suggestions.notes: Primary source texts are often found in collections or translations. The exact year for some primary documents can vary depending on the edition and translation. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and relevance to understanding Columbus's impact.
